newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says Lebed sacking will not harm Russia ties.
newsitem.headline: Japan says Lebed sacking will not harm Russia ties.

text.p: Japan reacted coolly on Friday to Russian President Boris Yeltsin's firing of his security chief Alexander Lebed, saying it would not affect bilateral ties between Tokyo and Moscow.
"The Japanese government does not think it will have significant impact on the relations between Japan and Russia," Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Teijiro Furukawa said.
Yeltsin announced on Thursday that he was dismissing Lebed from his top Kremlin post, accusing him of a lack of team spirit and open ambition to become the next president.
Lebed, 46, a straight-talking retired general who enjoys strong backing among the armed forces and is seen by many as the most trustworthy politician in Russia, called on his supporters to stay calm.
Japan is embroiled in a thorny dispute with Russia over a string of four small islands off northern Japan since Soviet troops seized them in the closing days of World War Two.
The dispute has stopped Tokyo, which calls the islands the Northern Territories, from providing large-scale financial aid to Russia or signing a formal peace treaty with Moscow.
Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov was expected to visit Tokyo in November to discuss bilateral ties with Japanese leaders.
"It (the sacking of Lebed) will not affect the diplomatic schedule involving the two countries," Furukawa told a news conference.
"We would like to watch the domestic situation in Russia," he added.
